Explore Kingston toilet paper holders in a variety of styles and finishes, including matte black, nickel, bronze, and brass. Choose a holder that fits your space and matches your bathroom. Make sure the toilet paper is easy to reach. For help choosing the right toilet paper holder for your project, call our Kitchen & Bath Experts toll-free at 1-877-252-7277. Toilet paper holders keep bathroom tissue within reach and give each roll a place of its own. You may also see these accessories called toilet tissue holders or toilet roll holders. Kingston offers styles and finishes for small powder rooms, guest baths, and main bathrooms. Explore options that work with your layout, match your fixtures, and make changing the roll simple. Start by choosing between a wall mount and a freestanding design. Then compare the size, finish, and mounting needs of each model. A well-chosen holder can bring the look of your bathroom accessories together while making your space easier to use. Choose a Mounting Style for Your Space Wall-Mount Toilet Paper Holders A wall-mount toilet paper holder attaches to a surface beside the toilet and keeps the floor clear. This can help in a narrow bathroom where there is little room for a stand. Some designs have one mounting post, while others use two. Check the full width and how far the holder extends from the wall. Leave enough room for a full roll, your hand, and nearby cabinet doors. If you attach the holder to a vanity, make sure the cabinet side is strong enough to hold it. Check that the screws will not block the drawers from opening or closing. Freestanding Toilet Paper Holders A freestanding toilet paper holder rests on the floor and can move when your layout changes. It can be useful when the nearest wall is too far away or you prefer to avoid drilling into tile. Measure the base before choosing a stand. It should fit beside the toilet without blocking the walkway. Some models also hold spare rolls, so check the storage details on the product page. Check Roll Size and Loading Style The holder needs to fit the toilet paper you use. A large roll may need more space between the rod and the wall than a smaller roll. Check both the usable rod length and the room around the roll. Also consider how you change the paper. An open-arm design lets you slide a roll onto the holder from one side. Other designs use a removable roller between two posts. Look at the product photos and instructions to understand how each model works. Check which side the roll slides on from, too. An open end placed against a wall or cabinet may leave too little room to remove the empty tube and add a new roll. For a shared bathroom, choose a style that everyone in your home can reach and reload comfortably. Find a Finish That Fits Your Bathroom A toilet paper holder can match your faucet or add another color to the room. Kingston offers finish options across the collection, including chrome, black, nickel, bronze, and brass tones. Available finishes vary by model. Consider these looks as you compare products: Polished chrome adds a bright, reflective touch. Matte black creates contrast against light walls or tile. Brushed nickel offers a softer metallic look. Oil rubbed bronze brings a darker tone to the room. Brass finishes add warmth, with polished and brushed options offering different levels of shine. Compare the full finish name when pairing pieces. Polished brass and brushed brass have different appearances, even though both belong to the same color family. Match Traditional or Modern Bathroom Styles Shape matters as much as finish. Rounded bases and decorative details can suit a traditional bathroom. Straight lines and simple shapes can work well in a modern space. Choose details that repeat the shapes already found in your faucet, mirror, or cabinet hardware. The Restoration BA3968C toilet paper holder has a traditional look. This polished chrome model has brass construction, a double-post design, and a 6¼-inch toilet paper rod. It also coordinates with other Restoration pieces. Use that example as a starting point, then compare each model’s measurements and features. A similar style does not always mean the same size or mounting layout. Measure and Plan the Location Choose a spot that feels comfortable to reach while seated. Before making holes, hold the paper roll near the planned location and check the space around it. Make sure it does not crowd your leg, touch the vanity, or block a drawer. When replacing an existing holder, compare the mounting points as well as the overall width. A new model may not cover the old holes. Check this before choosing based on appearance alone. Keep the roll away from places where it may get splashed. For more help comparing options, read Kingston’s Tips for Choosing a Toilet Paper Holder. Coordinate Your Bathroom Accessories Plan the holder alongside the other pieces you use each day. Matching finishes and similar shapes can help the room feel connected, even when you update only a few items. Pair your holder with towel bars for bath towels, towel rings near the sink, and robe hooks for extra hanging space. Choose sizes that fit each area without making the walls feel crowded. If you are also replacing your faucet, browse Kingston’s bathroom sink faucets while comparing finishes. Review the exact finish names and product images together before placing your order. Review Materials and Installation Details Check what the holder is made of and how to install it. A brass-colored finish describes the appearance; it does not, by itself, tell you what the holder is made from. Check whether mounting hardware is included and whether it suits your wall surface. Follow the product’s instructions for placement and attachment. If you choose a freestanding holder, check how to put it together. Make sure the base sits flat on the floor. Follow the care directions for your selected finish when cleaning. These details help you choose and look after the right model. Compare Kingston toilet paper holders by mounting style, size, finish, and daily use to find an option that fits your room. Toilet paper holders keep bathroom tissue within reach and give each roll a place of its own. You may also see these accessories called toilet tissue holders or toilet roll holders. Kingston offers styles and finishes for small powder rooms, guest baths, and main bathrooms. Explore options that work with your layout, match your fixtures, and make changing the roll simple. Start by choosing between a wall mount and a freestanding design. Then compare the size, finish, and mounting needs of each model. A well-chosen holder can bring the look of your bathroom accessories together while making your space easier to use. Choose a Mounting Style for Your Space Wall-Mount Toilet Paper Holders A wall-mount toilet paper holder attaches to a surface beside the toilet and keeps the floor clear. This can help in a narrow bathroom where there is little room for a stand. Some designs have one mounting post, while others use two. Check the full width and how far the holder extends from the wall. Leave enough room for a full roll, your hand, and nearby cabinet doors. If you attach the holder to a vanity, make sure the cabinet side is strong enough to hold it. Check that the screws will not block the drawers from opening or closing. Freestanding Toilet Paper Holders A freestanding toilet paper holder rests on the floor and can move when your layout changes. It can be useful when the nearest wall is too far away or you prefer to avoid drilling into tile. Measure the base before choosing a stand. It should fit beside the toilet without blocking the walkway. Some models also hold spare rolls, so check the storage details on the product page. Check Roll Size and Loading Style The holder needs to fit the toilet paper you use. A large roll may need more space between the rod and the wall than a smaller roll. Check both the usable rod length and the room around the roll. Also consider how you change the paper. An open-arm design lets you slide a roll onto the holder from one side. Other designs use a removable roller between two posts. Look at the product photos and instructions to understand how each model works. Check which side the roll slides on from, too. An open end placed against a wall or cabinet may leave too little room to remove the empty tube and add a new roll. For a shared bathroom, choose a style that everyone in your home can reach and reload comfortably. Find a Finish That Fits Your Bathroom A toilet paper holder can match your faucet or add another color to the room. Kingston offers finish options across the collection, including chrome, black, nickel, bronze, and brass tones. Available finishes vary by model. Consider these looks as you compare products: Polished chrome adds a bright, reflective touch. Matte black creates contrast against light walls or tile. Brushed nickel offers a softer metallic look. Oil rubbed bronze brings a darker tone to the room. Brass finishes add warmth, with polished and brushed options offering different levels of shine. Compare the full finish name when pairing pieces. Polished brass and brushed brass have different appearances, even though both belong to the same color family. Match Traditional or Modern Bathroom Styles Shape matters as much as finish. Rounded bases and decorative details can suit a traditional bathroom. Straight lines and simple shapes can work well in a modern space. Choose details that repeat the shapes already found in your faucet, mirror, or cabinet hardware. The Restoration BA3968C toilet paper holder has a traditional look. This polished chrome model has brass construction, a double-post design, and a 6¼-inch toilet paper rod. It also coordinates with other Restoration pieces. Use that example as a starting point, then compare each model’s measurements and features. A similar style does not always mean the same size or mounting layout. Measure and Plan the Location Choose a spot that feels comfortable to reach while seated. Before making holes, hold the paper roll near the planned location and check the space around it. Make sure it does not crowd your leg, touch the vanity, or block a drawer. When replacing an existing holder, compare the mounting points as well as the overall width. A new model may not cover the old holes. Check this before choosing based on appearance alone. Keep the roll away from places where it may get splashed. For more help comparing options, read Kingston’s Tips for Choosing a Toilet Paper Holder. Coordinate Your Bathroom Accessories Plan the holder alongside the other pieces you use each day. Matching finishes and similar shapes can help the room feel connected, even when you update only a few items. Pair your holder with towel bars for bath towels, towel rings near the sink, and robe hooks for extra hanging space. Choose sizes that fit each area without making the walls feel crowded. If you are also replacing your faucet, browse Kingston’s bathroom sink faucets while comparing finishes. Review the exact finish names and product images together before placing your order. Review Materials and Installation Details Check what the holder is made of and how to install it. A brass-colored finish describes the appearance; it does not, by itself, tell you what the holder is made from. Check whether mounting hardware is included and whether it suits your wall surface. Follow the product’s instructions for placement and attachment. If you choose a freestanding holder, check how to put it together. Make sure the base sits flat on the floor. Follow the care directions for your selected finish when cleaning. These details help you choose and look after the right model. Kingston offers toilet tank levers in many styles and finishes, including bronze, black, nickel, and brass, with options to match both modern and traditional bathroom designs. Call our Kitchen & Bath Experts toll-free at 1-877-252-7277 for help selecting the perfect Toilet Handle for your project. Toilet Tank Levers for Everyday Use A toilet tank lever is the handle assembly that starts a flush on a compatible toilet. Also called a toilet trip lever, it has an outside handle and an arm inside the tank. On many standard toilets, pressing the handle lifts a chain and opens the flapper. This lets water flow from the tank into the bowl. The handle is also a visible part of your bathroom. Choosing one that suits the room helps connect the toilet with nearby fixtures. Whether you are replacing a worn part or updating your space, start with the right fit and then choose the look you like. Find the Right Fit for Your Toilet Toilet tank levers are not all the same size or shape. Before ordering, compare your existing handle and tank with the product details. Check these points to help narrow your choices: Mounting position: Check whether the handle sits on the front or side of the tank. Choose a lever designed for that position. Tank opening: Compare the opening’s size and shape with the measurements listed for the replacement lever. Arm length and clearance: Make sure the inside arm has room to move without hitting other tank parts. Flush system: Confirm that the lever works with your toilet’s flushing system. Some models exclude dual-flush and pressure-assisted toilets. Kingston offers models for front mounting, plus options that support both front and side mounting. Even when a product is described as a universal toilet tank lever, check its listed fit requirements before buying. Keep your toilet’s brand and model number nearby when comparing products. Photos of the current handle and the inside of the tank can also help you explain what you need. For more help, read Kingston’s guide to choosing the best toilet tank lever for your bathroom. It explains how arm length, mounting style, and lever angle affect the handle’s fit. Select a Finish for Your Bathroom The finish helps your toilet handle blend in or stand out. Start with the metal finishes already used around your sink and shower. Polished chrome: A bright, reflective finish that pairs well with white fixtures and a wide range of bathroom colors. Brushed nickel: A softer metallic look that works well with neutral walls, natural textures, and simple bathroom hardware. Polished brass: A warm golden finish that can bring a classic touch to a bathroom or brighten a plain space. Oil rubbed bronze: A deep, warm finish that suits rustic details, wood cabinets, and many traditional bathroom designs. Matte black: A low-shine finish that creates contrast against a white toilet and pairs well with black faucets or accessories. Available finishes vary by model. Compare the finish name when shopping, since polished and brushed versions create different looks. Oil rubbed bronze can naturally develop a patina, or change in color, with use. The finish can look a little different on each piece. Comparing finish samples can help you choose a tone that works with your bathroom’s other fixtures and accessories. Choose Classic or Modern Toilet Handle Styles Kingston’s Victorian and Restoration designs offer classic details for traditional bathrooms. They can work well beside curved faucet handles, framed mirrors, and other pieces with a vintage feel. A decorative toilet handle can carry that style into a part of the room that is often overlooked. For a modern bathroom, explore the simple lines of Concord designs. A clean handle shape can suit a plain vanity and minimal accessories. Look at the shape as well as the finish. Rounded details can echo soft curves around the sink, while straighter lines can connect with square fixtures. Think about comfort, too. Choose a handle shape that feels practical for the people who use the bathroom. Check the product details for features that make the handle easier to use. Check What Comes with Your Replacement Handle Some products include a handle and trip lever arm, while others are replacement handles only. Read the product description to see which parts are included. A handle sold on its own must fit the connection on your existing arm. If your current arm still works, a compatible handle may be enough for a style update. If the arm is damaged, look for an assembly that includes the parts you need. Compare the material, measurements, and connection details before placing your order. Bring Your Bathroom Hardware Together A toilet tank lever is a small detail, but it can help the room feel more finished. Coordinate it with your bathroom faucets, towel bars, and toilet paper holders for a consistent look. You can also mix finishes with a clear plan. For example, repeat a black handle’s finish in a mirror frame or cabinet pulls. Browse Kingston bathroom accessories to find pieces that support your style. You can update a few small details without replacing your fixtures. Plan Your Toilet Handle Replacement A cracked handle, damaged arm, or lever that no longer moves properly may need attention. Check the cause before choosing replacement parts. A loose connection or chain problem may need an adjustment. Follow the instructions that come with your Kingston handle. After fitting the lever, check that the handle returns freely and the arm moves without catching. Flush the toilet to confirm that the connected parts work together. If you are unsure about the fit or repair, ask a qualified plumber for help. Care for Your Toilet Tank Lever Keep the handle clean with mild soap and a soft, damp cloth. Wipe away soap and dry the surface after cleaning. Avoid abrasive pads and cleaners containing bleach, ammonia, acids, or alcohol. Follow the care instructions supplied with your product to help protect its finish.
